# contextlake

> A local context layer for your AI tools: mirror your Git repositories, index them into a
> queryable knowledge graph + wiki, and serve it to AI editors over MCP. Offline-first, so
> agents answer from real source instead of guessing. Python CLI, published on PyPI.

## Understand it

- [Overview](https://sayak.in/contextlake/docs): A local context layer for your AI tools: mirror your repos, index them into a knowledge graph, and serve it over MCP.
- [contextlake, explained](https://sayak.in/contextlake/explained): What changes on your screen, the three layers underneath it, the design decisions and the alternatives they turned down, the confidence model, and the honest limits.
- [Benchmarks](https://sayak.in/contextlake/benchmarks): Where the token, cost, and correctness impact of connecting the contextlake MCP to your AI coding tools comes from, new-code grounding first, plus search, maintenance, the caveats, and how to measure it on your own repos.

## Get started

- [Installing and upgrading](https://sayak.in/contextlake/installing): Every way to install contextlake, pip, uv, pipx, Docker, or a standalone binary, plus the extras table, upgrading safely, and a clean uninstall.
- [Quickstart](https://sayak.in/contextlake/quickstart): Install, bootstrap, and wire your editor, the whole Mirror -> Knowledge -> Serve path in a few minutes.
- [Configuration](https://sayak.in/contextlake/configuration): Config-file precedence and the full settings reference for the mirror layer.

## Build your knowledge base

- [The knowledge layer](https://sayak.in/contextlake/knowledge-layer): Turn the mirror into a queryable graph with search, a wiki, and connectors.
- [Mirroring repositories](https://sayak.in/contextlake/mirroring-repositories): Mirror your Git repos locally and keep them fresh: fetch, clone, update, most-active branch, verify, and audit, with branch-safety guardrails.
- [Indexing the code graph](https://sayak.in/contextlake/indexing-the-code-graph): Turn your mirrored repos into a queryable code graph: incremental indexing, and the full node and edge model across 27 languages, Terraform, SQL, and web topology.
- [The code graph model](https://sayak.in/contextlake/code-graph-model): Every node kind and edge kind the parser emits, language by language, plus Terraform, SQL and web topology.
- [Connecting and enriching](https://sayak.in/contextlake/connecting-and-enriching): Link repos to their issues, docs, and designs, manage sources, and pull grounded external facts into the knowledge layer with query-driven enrichment.
- [Document sources and RAG](https://sayak.in/contextlake/document-sources): Configure the built-in files source, a plugin package or an MCP endpoint, and aggregate documents into the knowledge layer.
- [Searching semantically](https://sayak.in/contextlake/searching-semantically): Natural-language and hybrid graph-propagation retrieval: embed your code, tune the vector backend, and query across repos and languages.
- [Embeddings and models](https://sayak.in/contextlake/embedding-reference): What gets embedded, how a chunk is built, and which embedding model to pick for your hardware.
- [Generating the wiki](https://sayak.in/contextlake/generating-the-wiki): Turn the graph into grounded, council-verified prose per repo: searchable, enrichment-aware, with a provenance footer.
- [Generating documentation](https://sayak.in/contextlake/generating-documentation): An API reference straight from the graph, with every symbol's real call sites and no model involved.
- [What the generator produces](https://sayak.in/contextlake/generated-docs-reference): Section by section, what lands in the API reference, the design notes and the fleet page.

## Use it

- [Asking the graph](https://sayak.in/contextlake/asking-the-graph): Search the graph from the terminal, trace what a change would break, and find who to ask: `kb query`, `kb impact`, and `kb owners`.
- [Serving over MCP](https://sayak.in/contextlake/serving-over-mcp): Expose the knowledge layer over MCP and wire your editors (Claude Code, Windsurf, Kiro) in one command.
- [MCP transports and limits](https://sayak.in/contextlake/mcp-transports): stdio, HTTP and SSE side by side, how many tool calls run at once, and the provenance every cited node carries.
- [Using the dashboard](https://sayak.in/contextlake/using-the-dashboard): A guided tour of the local, offline-first dashboard: the fleet overview, per-repo anatomy, the architecture graph, blast radius, and generating a wiki.
- [Visualizing the graph](https://sayak.in/contextlake/visualizing-the-graph): Draw bounded, offline graph slices (`contextlake kb graph`) in any of 11 formats, HTML, DOT, JSON, GraphML, Cypher and six Mermaid diagram types, plus the composed namespace C4 diagram.

## Operate it

- [Keeping it fresh](https://sayak.in/contextlake/keeping-it-fresh): Run the whole pipeline in one command, schedule it, re-index on commit with a git hook, and watch an unattended run.
- [Scheduling runs](https://sayak.in/contextlake/scheduling): Measure a run, work out an interval, and install a systemd timer or crontab entry that keeps it current on its own, set/reset/unset, ad-hoc jobs, and the interval formula.
- [Console output](https://sayak.in/contextlake/console-output): Decode the progress bar, the status glyph vocabulary, the JSON logs, the stdout/stderr split, and the four exit codes.
- [Troubleshooting](https://sayak.in/contextlake/troubleshooting): Install and mirror problems that have actually been hit, each with the fix and the reason behind it.

## Reference

- [Architecture and internals](https://sayak.in/contextlake/internals): How all three layers work inside: the store on disk, concurrency, branch selection, versioning and staleness, and the two invariants.
- [Command reference](https://sayak.in/contextlake/cli-reference): Every contextlake command at a glance, with links to the page that documents each in depth.
- [Model providers](https://sayak.in/contextlake/model-providers): The pluggable embeddings and wiki backends: auto, built-in CPU, Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, and agent-CLI, with data-sharing posture and setup.
- [Changelog](https://sayak.in/contextlake/changelog): Release history for contextlake.

## Project

- [Writing style](https://sayak.in/contextlake/style-guide): The spirit, the checklist, and links to the focused pages: voice, structure, formatting, and the word reference.
- [Voice and tone](https://sayak.in/contextlake/style-guide-voice): Second person, present tense, warm and grounded: the voice defaults, word choice, and writing for every reader.
- [Page types and structure](https://sayak.in/contextlake/style-guide-structure): The concept, how-to, reference, and tutorial page types, each with a fixed skeleton, and how to structure a page.
- [Formatting](https://sayak.in/contextlake/style-guide-formatting): Headings, lists, code, callouts, links, accessibility, and inclusive language: the mechanics that keep every page consistent.
- [Word reference](https://sayak.in/contextlake/style-guide-reference): The house-style decision cache, before and after rewrites, and the A-to-Z term reference.
- [Brand overview](https://sayak.in/contextlake/brand): contextlake's brand in one page: essence, voice, the lake metaphor, Pebble, the palette, and the mark, with the full spec linked.
- [Adding a language](https://sayak.in/contextlake/adding-a-language): The ordered contributor recipe for teaching contextlake a new source language: the nine edits, the parts to leave alone, and the commands that prove the grammar works.
